claims.description: Commands applied to the FSM and reported successfully to clients have the durable replication support required by the applicable cluster configuration.

scope.description: The ordinary Apply path from log replication through commitment and FSM completion.
excluded: No claim that an unsuccessful Apply had no effect

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Establish configuration transition rules, durability contracts, and the complete commitment-to-FSM handoff.

grounding.derivation: The Apply documentation describes durable quorum commitment before FSM application, and FSM.Apply's interface comment states that application follows majority commitment. These statements supply an attributed expectation. The observed commitment calculator and follower acknowledgement path identify supporting responsibilities but do not establish the complete guarantee.
grounding.applicability: Applies to ordinary command application. Voter selection, leader context, storage durability and completion correspondence must be established separately.
unresolved: The leader's dispatch and commit-consumption paths are unread.
Storage backend guarantees and legal membership transitions are not established.
alternatives: Snapshot transfer can establish replication progress when logs have been compacted.

claims.description: Within one commitment instance, each commit-index advance must be supported by a strict majority of the currently tracked voters' reported match indexes and must reach startIndex; match reports must not decrease stored progress and commitIndex must not decrease.

scope.description: The commitment component's calculation over reported progress, including voter-map replacement.
assumptions: Operations obey the component's mutex discipline.
excluded: Truth and durability of match reports

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Historical support under membership changes remains outside this local obligation.

grounding.derivation: The component comments explicitly assign it responsibility for monotonically advancing the leader's commit index from voter disk progress and identify startIndex as a prerequisite. Its callers consume the resulting index. The proposed check independently expresses that responsibility over reported values; it does not assume those reports represent durable storage.
grounding.applicability: Directly applicable to newCommitment, match, setConfiguration and recalculate. An unchanged historical commitIndex need not acquire fresh support under every replacement voter map; this obligation constrains advances.
unresolved: Caller guarantees for startIndex and configuration sequencing are not established.
alternatives: Previously achieved commitment can remain monotonic after configuration replacement without a new advance.

claims.description: Progress supplied to commitment must identify the reporting server and a prefix that agrees with the leader's log and satisfies the applicable persistence contract.

scope.description: Production of match progress from local writes, AppendEntries responses and snapshot catch-up.
excluded: Byzantine peer behavior unless subsequently supported by a fault contract

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Read updateLastAppended and the local-write producer.
Establish transport response correlation and storage failure semantics.
Explore pipeline and snapshot progress updates.

grounding.derivation: commitment.match's comment requires disk agreement through the reported index. replicateTo consumes successful AppendEntries responses through updateLastAppended. appendEntries checks a preceding log term, handles conflicts and stores new entries before success. This producer-consumer dependency supports a candidate obligation, while the missing helper and backend contracts prevent treating the guarantee as established.
grounding.applicability: Relevant wherever progress contributes to commitment. The supplied code establishes the ordinary RPC path only partially.
unresolved: The updateLastAppended call is not a resolved callee binding.
Successful storage return has no supplied durability or partial-failure contract.
Request construction and response identity guarantees are unread.
conflicts: appendEntries explicitly notes stale last-log state after successful truncation followed by failed StoreLogs; its subsequent consequences are unestablished.
alternatives: Snapshot installation supplies an alternative catch-up mechanism.
Pipelined replication has a separate completion path.

claims.description: Snapshot-based recovery preserves a coherent FSM prefix and corresponding Raft configuration when replacing compacted log history.

scope.description: Automatic snapshot capture, publication, compaction and startup restoration.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Establish snapshot capture metadata, store publication guarantees, compaction boundaries and recovery replay behavior.

grounding.derivation: README describes restoration as equivalent to replay of the captured history. The FSM interface assigns capture and persistence responsibilities. takeSnapshot writes prefix and configuration metadata, while restoreSnapshot consumes it to suppress replay and initialize configuration. Their dependency makes metadata coherence externally significant.
grounding.applicability: Default restoration and NoSnapshotRestoreOnStart require distinct treatment: the latter explicitly delegates FSM recovery to another mechanism while retaining metadata initialization.
unresolved: The external recovery obligation when NoSnapshotRestoreOnStart is enabled is not specified here.
alternatives: An application may recover its FSM through a separate mechanism under NoSnapshotRestoreOnStart.

claims.description: takeSnapshot must reject a captured prefix older than the selected committed configuration and must not advertise its last-snapshot metadata or begin compaction before snapshot persistence and sink closure both succeed.

scope.description: The snapshot coordinator's metadata compatibility guard and publication ordering.
excluded: Accuracy of the supplied FSM prefix
Historical correctness of the supplied committed configuration

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Resolve the producer and storage contracts before extending this obligation to recoverability.

grounding.derivation: The configurations comment explains that only two configurations are retained and a snapshot behind committedIndex cannot be represented. Recovery subsequently trusts the stored snapshot index and configuration. The coordinator's guard and persist/close ordering are therefore candidate obligations supporting that consumer, independently of whether its inputs and storage implementation are sound.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the observed takeSnapshot path, including persistence and closure errors. It is a local ordering obligation, not a proof that a published snapshot is recoverable.
unresolved: SnapshotSink.Close and repeated-close behavior are unread.
The snapshot future's index/term production is only partially supplied.
alternatives: The coordinator can reject a snapshot and retain logs until a compatible FSM prefix is available.

associations.rationale: Initializes voter progress and the first-index threshold for one commitment instance.

bindings.description: Creates zero-valued match indexes only for voters and retains supplied startIndex.
pending: Caller initialization and configuration validation are unread.

associations.rationale: Replaces the voter set while retaining progress for surviving server IDs.

bindings.description: Rebuilds the map under lock and recalculates commitment.
pending: The call site's membership transition eligibility is not established.

associations.rationale: Filters progress reports by voter membership and strictly increasing index.

bindings.description: Updates a tracked voter's progress only when the report increases its stored index.
pending: The reported prefix's identity and durability are separate producer obligations.

associations.rationale: Computes majority-supported progress and applies the advancement threshold.

bindings.description: Sorts reported indexes, selects the strict-majority threshold, and advances only above the previous index and at or beyond startIndex.
pending: Notification delivery semantics are not included in the local arithmetic check.

associations.rationale: Consumes a successful follower response at the progress-update boundary.

bindings.description: Constructs and sends AppendEntries, rejects newer response terms, processes success through updateLastAppended, and falls back to snapshots when a log is unavailable.
pending: Request construction, updateLastAppended and snapshot progress production remain unresolved callees.

associations.rationale: Produces the follower acknowledgement consumed as replication support.

bindings.description: Checks term and preceding-log compatibility, truncates conflicts, stores new entries, processes configuration and commit updates, then reports success.
pending: StoreLogs and DeleteRange failure semantics are unread.
Legal request construction and snapshot-aware last-index behavior remain open.

associations.rationale: Checks configuration-prefix compatibility and sequences persistence, publication and compaction.

bindings.description: Rejects a snapshot behind committedIndex; creates and persists a sink, checks Close, publishes last-snapshot metadata, then invokes compaction.
pending: Snapshot future, sink and compaction contracts require additional material.

associations.rationale: Shows why published snapshot metadata affects recovery and skipped replay.

bindings.description: Selects a restorable snapshot, installs its applied and stable-snapshot indexes, and initializes committed and latest configurations.
pending: Snapshot listing order, startup replay and alternate FSM recovery need separate investigation.

relations.rationale: Correct calculation over reported progress is one necessary component of the broader application guarantee.
pending: This relation does not make the local obligation sufficient for G_apply.

grounding.derivation: The documented Apply path consumes advancement produced by the commitment component.
unresolved: The actual leader-loop handoff remains unread.

relations.rationale: Numerically sufficient reports support durable application only if their underlying replication evidence is sound.

grounding.derivation: The match contract interprets reports as disk agreement, and the ordinary replication path derives progress from follower success.
grounding.applicability: Local and remote progress contributing to leader commitment.
unresolved: Local-write, pipeline and snapshot producers are not fully read.
alternatives: Snapshot catch-up may replace ordinary log replication.

relations.rationale: The calculator consumes reported match indexes whose durable-prefix meaning is not established by its own implementation.
pending: Resolve producers before extending the local result to durable quorum support.

grounding.derivation: match checks voter membership and increasing numbers, while its comment assigns a stronger meaning to those numbers.
grounding.applicability: All match reports used by the commitment component.
unresolved: Acknowledgement correlation and durability remain unverified.
alternatives: Different producers may establish equivalent prefix support through logs or snapshots.

relations.rationale: Recovery consumes the snapshot metadata whose compatibility and publication order the coordinator controls.
pending: Capture accuracy, durable storage and recovery replay remain additional obligations.

grounding.derivation: Publishing incompatible metadata or compacting before successful persistence could invalidate the history recovery expects to reconstruct.
grounding.applicability: Automatic snapshot production consumed by startup recovery.
unresolved: The full recovery and compaction contracts are not supplied.
alternatives: Configured external FSM recovery changes the restoration boundary.
